y1: The wise men were scholars from the area of modern-day Iran and Iraq. They studied stars and dreams. They were not Jews, but Gentiles.
y2: Surprisingly, the first to seek and find the Messiah were not the Jews who knew the Bible well, but Gentiles from a faraway country. Just as Matthew included Gentile women in the genealogy in the first chapter, here too he shows that Jesus is the King of all nations.
y3: Numbers 24:17 says, “A star will come out of Jacob.” God guided the men who studied stars in a way they could understand, and finally led them to Jesus through His Word.
y5: King Herod was a king appointed by Rome. He was so suspicious that he would even kill his own family to protect his throne. The birth of the “King of the Jews” was a threat to him.
y6: The chief priests and teachers of the law whom Herod gathered knew the word of the prophet Micah well: the Messiah would be born in Bethlehem. But not one of them went to Bethlehem, which was only 9 kilometers away.
y7: Scholars who knew the Word but didn't move; wise men who knew little but traveled a long way. Faith doesn't end with knowing; it continues with steps taken toward Jesus.
y9: When the star stopped over the house where the baby was, the wise men rejoiced with exceedingly great joy. They bowed down, worshiped, and gave gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
y10: For a long time, these gifts have been explained as signs showing who Jesus is.
y11: Gold was given to kings, frankincense was burned in worship to God, and myrrh was used in burials. Therefore, much of Christian tradition explains these gifts like this: Jesus the King, Jesus who is God, and Jesus who would die for us.
y13: God warned the wise men in a dream not to return to Herod. They went back to their own country by another way.
y14: A person who meets Jesus does not go back the same way. After this meeting, the direction of life changes.
verse: “They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary his mother, and they fell down and worshiped Him. Opening their treasures, they offered Him gifts.”
prayer: Lord God, we thank You for the grace of calling even people from faraway countries to worship Jesus. Help us not to be satisfied with just knowing, but to go toward Jesus. I give the throne of my life to Jesus. I pray in the name of King Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: wise men. They were scholars in the region of Persia and Babylon who studied stars and dreams. They were educated men, not kings. Matthew describes them as people searching for the truth.
d1: Gentile. It refers to all nations outside of Israel, God's covenant people. The Gospel of Matthew begins with Gentile wise men and ends with the command to “make disciples of all nations” (28:19).
d2: Herod. He was a capable king who rebuilt the great temple, but because of his suspicion, he even killed his wife and sons. At that time, people used to say, “It is better to be Herod's pig than his son.”
d3: chief priest. They were the priests responsible for worship in the temple and leading the people. The chief priests appear again at Jesus' trial (Chapter 26).
d4: Micah. He is a prophet who lived in the 8th century BC. He said that the One who would lead Israel would come from Bethlehem. “But you, Bethlehem... are not the least” (Mic. 5:2).
d5: worship. It actually means “to bow down and kiss”. It was a show of total respect before a king. In the Gospel of Matthew, this word is used for Jesus many times. It shows that Jesus is worthy of worship.
d6: frankincense. It is the resin of the frankincense tree. When burned, it gives off sweet-smelling smoke, and was used in temple worship. Frankincense was also in the holy incense in Exodus chapter 30.
d7: myrrh. It is a fragrant oil made from the resin of the myrrh tree. It was used when burying the dead. Myrrh was also used when Jesus was taken down from the cross (John 19:39).
